subject: Financify: sudden spike in Hosted API initial-response p95/p99 — urgent
messages:
From: Platform Ops <ops@financify.com>

Date: Mon, 09 Mar 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Production alert — sudden p95/p99 jump (Financify)

Hey Tessa,

We're seeing a significant regression on the Hosted API calls from our production cluster over the last 45m: p95 for initial-response (first-token) rose from ~120ms to ~980ms, and p99 is hitting ~2.8s. Error rate has crept up to 1.4% (mostly 503s during bursts). This began around 14:20 UTC.

We captured traces and a short Flamegraph — attaching. Can you triage? This is impacting our realtime workflow and we've started throttling upstream to avoid cascading failures.

Attaching: p95-p99-traces.zip (9.2MB)

--
Sanjay Rao

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>

Cc: Platform Ops <ops@financify.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Mar 2026 08:48:05 -0700
Subject: Re: Production alert — sudden p95/p99 jump (Financify)

Quick diagnostic from infra side (summary):
- Correlation: multiple GPU pool replenish events at ~14:17–14:22 UTC (pool id: hosted-us-west-2-fin-87). Cold node attach latency aligned with p95 spikes.
- Root cause hypothesis: kernel selection fallback on startup for quantized kernels — when a newly provisioned node initializes, we observed falling back to a compatibility kernel path (generic cuBLAS) for certain fused attention ops. That fallback adds ~600–1200ms per initialization step across the first few tokens.
- Additional signal: warm_pool_evictions spiked due to a short-lived host-side OOM during health checks; the autoscaler then provisioned nodes in reaction to increased queued requests.

Immediate mitigations I can apply (temporary):
- Force pin the model to quantized_v2 variant for this customer's route (avoids kernel negotiation overhead).
- Set warm_min_nodes=2 for the customer pool and enable pre_warm_override=true for 30 minutes.
- Disable the new heuristic that reduces warm pool retention (roll back the recent change we shipped last night).

I'll push the pin + warm_min change if you authorize. Expect measurement within ~10–15 minutes after change: p95 should fall back close to baseline.

Attachment: trace_analysis.csv (sample init timings)

-David
Senior SRE, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Platform Ops <ops@financify.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Mar 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Production alert — sudden p95/p99 jump (Financify) — mitigation plan

Sanjay — thanks for the quick signal. We have a short mitigation plan and an ETA:

What we'll do now (09:05 PT):
- David will pin the route to quantized_v2 and set warm_min_nodes=2 for the pool.
- We'll enable pre_warm_override=true for 30 minutes to give extra warm capacity.
- We'll also roll back the warm-pool retention tweak that appears to have increased churn.

Expected impact: we expect p95 to fall from ~980ms back toward baseline (~<200ms) within ~12 minutes (after node warm caches populate). p99 should reduce in the subsequent 20–30 minutes.

Risk/notes: this is a targeted change for Financify's pool only. We will monitor token-level error rates and CPU/GPU utilization. If you have a maintenance window preference, tell us now — otherwise we'll proceed immediately.

I'll send a brief exec-facing note once we confirm recovery.

Thanks,
Tessa
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: Platform Ops <ops@financify.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Production alert — sudden p95/p99 jump (Financify)

Thanks — changes applied on your signal. Observed p95 drop to ~160ms within 10 minutes and p99 down to ~480ms within 25 minutes. Error rate back to 0.1%. We'll keep elevated traffic now and report any regression.

Appreciate the quick turnaround and please send your postmortem when available.

– Sanjay
